item.title: Blacklist for all >:)
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description: So I took a peek at the weblogs just now, having been deeply troubled by the fact that Google *still* hasn't updated the snippet to my Perl CPAN module page (ugh! Search engines can be so annoying...) and I discovered in the 1-megabyte 3000-ish logs for yizx.net today (I made them rotate daily that is), there were these incessant php requests over and over again. Like if you are a human (because this guy clearly wasn't), for reference, that is the equivalent of running a bloated Javascript-loaded web app! (looking at you JS frameworks...) My site has none of that, yet it is getting that treatment. It's just unfair... And because my manual regex "filters" aren't sensitive enough to pick up on this delinquent behavior (and I don't have any rate limiting policy, sigh...) this guy just escaped, as if it never did anything wrong. But I wasn't letting them go... at least, when I picked one of them up this time, I actually put it in a ban-list lookup. And guess what? It is banned on four of those lists! https://mxtoolbox.com/SuperTool.aspx?action=blacklist%3a129.153.203.128&run=toolpage Blacklist Reason TTL ====== ============ ========================== ==== LISTED BLOCKLIST.DE 129.153.203.128 was listed 2100 LISTED DRONE BL 129.153.203.128 was listed 300 LISTED s5h.net 129.153.203.128 was listed 5 LISTED Spamhaus ZEN 129.153.203.128 was listed 300 And then I realized -- wait a minute, there are people who curate specific ban lists like these *FOR* me! I don't even have to think about sifting through thousands of logs- how did i- aghhh!!! o///o (ok don't ask me how but I never thought thousands of "deny IP;" rules of nginx rules would be viable ok =_= Like, you gotta think about how this scales. And obviously anything linear in lookup time would be absurd to use to deal with something with this scale.) Right now I am using "ipsum"[1] because I found it from one search to another and it introduced me to ipset, which has this cool thing that matches IPs with a hash table. We'll see how it goes out from here :) [1]: https://github.com/stamparm/ipsum?tab=readme-ov-file Generally I don't think anyone should have to worry about their IPs ending up on these lists, unless someone who you happen to live near and happens to use your network to do shady stuff... happens to be on your network, well. You can try finding yourself on the list, or ask me to look it up for you in this "ipsum" hash table... Either way, that's all you need to know!

item.title: Nginx httpd did not start....
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
Installing Apache HTTPD a while ago (*while* I have nginx, yes, I wanted to see its directory listing icons which were quite fancy compared to Nginx (which erm, has none)) caused the unit to be enabled by default, which I missed so after my previous reboot, apache2.service was running while nginx.service... well. It could not start at all, because port 80 was taken.
Disabled apache2.service just now so this shouldn't be a problem anymore... (I will be honest, I had no idea that the site was down because the server itself wasn't lol)
I went over to Uptime Robot (which I have been messing around with for a while) and it said that the time it took between my reboot and me getting some sleep afterwards was um... "9 hours and 59 minutes". Well, um.... I explained why that happened anyways.
And I know we've been quite a lot of visits since I put my website out there on CPAN (judging by that we got indexed by Google at least (which I do *not* like to be quite honest -- it's incomplete page that I don't have any time to fix now since school has been a train wreck ToT)) so if you are a human coming from there -- sorry about that!

item.title: Renewed!
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
Phew we're back... I guess. All it took was an extra "listen [::]:80" because Certbot really was adamant about checking if my server was reachable via IPv6. I guess it's because IPv6 didn't match any of the nginx virtual server blocks so it went straight to my catch-all fallback server that USUALLY denies requests that don't provide an HTTP/1.1 Host header... but this time it denied valid requests that simply use IPv6 and not the IPv4 it knows.
I'm just, so weirded out -- like what @_@ Either way uh I ran certbot renew and the post-renewal hook basically brought all the sites back (it did completely ignore that my pre-renewal hook complained with an error code, but... whatever i guess >_>) Right now I'm just reeling in the madness i just witnessed, of my own site falling apart completely because i didn't take that Let's Encrypt email about expiration (that i did NOT expect was due to the auto-renewal not running correctly!) so seriously.....
But well, lesson learned: Certbot does look at your IPv6. I won't be dismissing that tiny [::]:80 and tiny [::]:443 anymore from now on....

item.title: Certificate for www.rapidcow.org just expired
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org

Weird that it automatically renewed just fine in March but now it's freaking out? But well, fair enough, I've never read the certbot renewal logs once, and I am just re-learning how to run the most basic certbot commands again.
Though, I believe the effects aren't too much -- I was just showing my mom the site this morning! I've just been drawing all day that I didn't get a chance to see this. Please be patient while I obtain a new SSL certificate!

item.title: www.yizx.net got TCP RST treatment in China???
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
Pardon me for the lazy pre text again (no pun intended), but I
    think I must talk about this.... I thought it was my SSL renewal
    that didn't trigger properly when I tried to access www.yizx.net
    on Firefox but got this:

    = Secure Connection Failed
    An error occurred during a connection to www.yizx.net.
    Error code: PR_CONNECT_RESET_ERROR

    Indeed there seems to be some kind of funky TCP thing
    that just hangs me up for no good reason...

    $ curl -vL http://www.yizx.net
    * Host www.yizx.net:80 was resolved.
    * IPv6: (none)
    * IPv4: 164.90.136.30
    *   Trying 164.90.136.30:80...
    * Connected to www.yizx.net (164.90.136.30) port 80
    > GET / HTTP/1.1
    > Host: www.yizx.net
    > User-Agent: curl/8.7.1
    > Accept: */*
    >
    * Request completely sent off
    * Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
    * Closing connection
    curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer

    $ curl -vL https://www.yizx.net
    * Host www.yizx.net:443 was resolved.
    * IPv6: (none)
    * IPv4: 164.90.136.30
    *   Trying 164.90.136.30:443...
    * Connected to www.yizx.net (164.90.136.30) port 443
    * ALPN: curl offers h2,http/1.1
    * (304) (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
    *  CAfile: /etc/ssl/cert.pem
    *  CApath: none
    * Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
    * LibreSSL/3.3.6: error:02FFF036:system library:func(4095):Connection reset by peer
    * Closing connection
    curl: (35) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer

    But I tried to connect from the server itself, on my
    phone tunneled through a VPN... it seems to be fine
    UNLESS I try to do it direct on my home Wi-Fi.
    (Dad prolly removed the router proxy while I was in uni, so
    I am connected to the raw, unfiltered network in China.)

    I guess I never noticed it, maybe China had banned my domain
    because of its history with hosting questionable "entertainment"
    videos...  I'm not quite sure what to do here.

    One weird thing: I guess if I type slowly enough (that is, I use
    telnet(1) to make a TCP connection and type the request myself),
    then I have some chance of connecting to HTTP over port 80.
    But if I use standard HTTP clients: curl, wget, HTTP::Tiny, then
    I get ECONNRESET (errno 54, Connection reset by peer).  It's as
    if someone is sitting between my router and the ISP, watching
    the TCP packets I send... it only gets tired of watching after
    like 5 seconds, or if I time my escape correctly, 1/10 of a second
    works as well.  But these naive clients sending out the request
    as quickly as they can all get sniped by a TCP RST with utmost
    precision in their forehead.  In fact, this is such a blatant MITM
    thing that I can see while my socket client gets a TCP reset, my
    server sends out the response and dutifully records in the access
    log a successful 301 redirection.

    And I have been testing port 80 (HTTP) only because I don't get a
    chance to connect over TLS due to...

    $ openssl s_client -crlf -nocommands -connect www.yizx.net:443
    Connecting to 164.90.136.30
    CONNECTED(00000005)
    write:errno=54
    ---
    no peer certificate available
    ---
    No client certificate CA names sent
    Negotiated TLS1.3 group: <NULL>
    ---
    SSL handshake has read 0 bytes and written 1545 bytes
    Verification: OK
    ---
    New, (NONE), Cipher is (NONE)
    Protocol: TLSv1.3
    This TLS version forbids renegotiation.
    Compression: NONE
    Expansion: NONE
    No ALPN negotiated
    Early data was not sent
    Verify return code: 0 (ok)
    ---

    You guessed it, errno=54 in tiny print... it's ECONNRESET again!
    The only way around this with my limited knowledge of SSL is by
    connecting to say, rapidcow.org, that I *know* is hosted by the
    same server as the one hosting yizx.net:

    $ openssl s_client -crlf -nocommands -quiet -connect www.rapidcow.org:443
    Connecting to 164.90.136.30
    depth=2 C=US, O=Internet Security Research Group, CN=ISRG Root X1
    verify return:1
    depth=1 C=US, O=Let's Encrypt, CN=E6
    verify return:1
    depth=0 CN=www.rapidcow.org
    verify return:1
    GET / HTTP/1.1
    Host: www.yizx.net
    User-Agent: very tired ethan... =,=;
    Accept: */*
    Connection: close

    HTTP/1.1 200 OK
    Server: nginx/1.24.0 (Ubuntu)
    Date: Sun, 25 May 2025 17:46:19 GMT
    Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
    Content-Length: 622
    Last-Modified: Sat, 25 Jan 2025 19:36:27 GMT
    Connection: close
    ETag: "67953d3b-26e"
    Accept-Ranges: bytes

    hiya!!! welcome to www.yizx.net!!!

    if you see this, then i'm putting pieces together!

    if you are looking for specific content (e.g. the binary
    search blog), i am aware.... it'll come back when i figure
    out how to set up my web server. so plz be patient.... :(

    P.S. i am the owner of yizx.net since November 2023.
    any content created before this point IS NOT MY WORK.
    i only learned such content recently through the wayback
    machine, and i promise that i won't let such content
    show up again while i'm in charge.

    in the meantime... be civil. kindly stop requesting those
    "content", because you won't find them here. ;)

    So yeah... that's two hours of my life spent figuring out if
    I misconfigured something.  Turns out it was just the GFW
    meddling with my sanity and my will to live in China.  It seems
    like I have to migrate what was on www.yizx.net to blog.yizz.me
    or something like that, if I want my friends here to read them...

item.title: Infrastructure update
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
It's a little bit late to say this, but I've started
    proxying some of my "big" sites through Anubis[1].
    (For those who are not aware of Anubis, it's basically
    an HTTP proxy that should do a better job at blocking
    web scraping bots than my Fail2ban filter can be.)

    Okay, nobody has really noticed this, is there?
    But that's okay, I'll just tell you what happened...

     * www.endfindme.com was the first "lab rat" that
       first got put behind the Anubis proxy:

       commit ed468e5b435ac4fe4884456d553002b19de90036
       Date:   Mon Apr 28 09:48:34 2025 -0500

           try out this anubis thing

           yooooo it really works :D

           (and just before my class time, nice!)

       (My math class starts at 10 am, so I did make it :)

     * Then I published the new www.rapidcow.org I've kept
       in my Git repository for a while (by that I mean...
       three full months ago, from the start of February.)

       commit 74d33bfaa6ce082ab572b86bbd1fec337647222a
       Date:   Sat May 3 18:46:08 2025 -0500

           configure www.rapidcow.org

     * Within about one hour, I noticed that my Nginx sub-server
       running on port 3000 was redirecting URLs to its own port,
       making redirects on the "active" servers hang indefinitely:

       commit 162a15f0131902db0bf0ad94f7de8e23c8852084
       Date:   Sat May 3 19:49:57 2025 -0500

           ack!!! do not forward people to port 3000!!!

           it is a good thing they are behind firewall....

       (By active, I just mean sites that have more than an index.txt,
       which used to be that "blue screen" with me floating midair but
       that is long gone because I don't want to waste bandwidth =_=
       (I swear I've talked about this... I am just repeating in case
       by the slimmest chance anyone new comes by; I am still 99% the
       only human visitor to my websites are me, myself, and I.))

    Here are a few more things I should update with:

    1. Since this site has been hosted on SourceHut Pages for a
       while now, I don't really feel obligated in making the full
       history of these status on Codeberg updates available in
       form of a Git repository.  This is done in anticipation of
       expiring my older status updates.  Besides I never enjoy the
       thought of people reading my mind without going through me...
       (To be content with that you'd have to be either dead and/or
       famous -- and I'm neither!)

       There is a broken link to Codeberg in 1734362640.
       It will be disabled shortly after I post this update.

    2. Regarding the previous update (1742319000): I have intermittently
       written posts on the CSL user page and have not touched the
       current state of www.endfindme.com in any way.  But even *then*,
       I must pause whatever I am doing.  I have in my course evaluation
       form (glad they still do that...) included a link to a not-yet-
       existent page at https://www.endfindme.com/cs400/critique/. But
       it is up to the CS400 professors + staff if they want to take my...
       hard-pressed unforgiving criticism.  (I don't know, maybe there is
       just something about learning to program by yourself that prevents
       you from accepting clear, narrow-minded nonsense they spoon-feed
       you about how stuff works, compared to people who are just accept
       ing it because they believe everything that the professors say.)

    3. This status update has no effort in HTML markup.  For those
       of you on RSS reader, sorry; but I won't have time to fix it
       until my exam, homework, and dormitory move-out are settled...

item.title: Planned Update
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
Hello Netizens. It's been a while I know. I don't have much to say except CS400 sucks... I haven't got the time to do anything. I am barely handing in my other homework because everything snowballed ever since I had to review three other people's code. (And if you are the one person who has seen the sole code review I have ever written, you'll know why I never got to complete just one review.)

Thank goodness it is just about to be over and I will have some time to roast about their abysmal course structure. Hopefully it won't ambush me with the next project or something like that (which is about making Web and GUI applications which, I'm not particularly excited about. As long as they don't force us to use anything monolithic or expect us to squeeze everything in one class I should be... relatively fine.)

I will be putting the goodies on www.endfindme.com though (which is perfect for keep the angry "dry" boring stuff out of my main web sites, but not quite "impersonal" enough to be managed by someone else's domain/web server ;) since they seem to want us to "submit" the next project's stuff through the CSL user pages at pages.cs.wisc.edu/~user/. Their submission model has always been sketchy as heck since they stopped using the tested-and-tried Gradescope, but I'll rant about all that in one go. Also, I use the word "submit" even though I've yet checked the relevant course instruction pages if that is the medium through which they want us to present our work. I just happened to stumble upon an impressive array of student-made "web sites" the other day I was navigating the public course directory in the CSL Ubuntu machine. They are like a graveyard of dead HTML pages that served one purpose (that was likely the same reason that brought them here) and ceased to be useful since. With the chilling wind blowing through tombtones, engraved with the names of their previous owner, once eminating beams of life, now hauled indifferently into the abyss, and trapped in this bleak directory of nowhere. The files that live on in this strange kind of limbo but will never become what it was, carrying nothing but the temporary memories and bits it survived for...

Sorry, I am simply inclined to say such stuff about the copius amounts of code and other things they had us write, but will never have a second chance to see the light of the day. It saddens me to see that this is the way things are in school assignments, in proprietary code bases (from what I've heard). How people could write stuff only to part with it for good. Of course my concern is less about the stuff they wrote because they're, uh, trash anyways. :D But I don't like that happen to my code. My code is my voice... and I don't like being trapped. Which is kind of the whole reason I make web sites, instead of trying to get a proper Instagram account and follow every person I've interacted with. (Or a YouTube channel where I yap about stuff as I know everything... that sounds fun, sure. >_>)

~RC (since it's been a while, I'll do a proper sign-off...)

P.S. Yes, I do have YouTube, and I do still have an idea of what I want to upload. But I will do that sparingly since they now have AI video summaries, and... you know. I want the context stuff on my web site and treat YouTube more like a CDN than a self-contained source of truth. There is an IndieWeb wiki page about this.

item.title: I forgot to turn nginx on - sorry!
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
For a while I have been wondering why the server has been refusing connections even though my firewall didn't block the IP I was connecting from... well turns out nginx wasn't running this whole time :x

Sorry for the confusion if anyone thought the server was down! Also let me know my firewall rules are too strict for you... I understand that IP bans can be quite unfair to people who actually want to access my website but can't because a few bad actors taint the IP reputation. If you are patient know that the IP bans aren't permanent (as long my ban wears them out -- which is the real point of banning! I promise it's not because I hate people, but bots… are annoying. >:c)

item.title: Server Operational!
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
Hey so just to let you know I've been leaving my server to handle HTTP/S requests for www.rapidcow.org and friends for a while now! Got new SSL certificates with certbot, also learned how to use Fail2ban so IPs that spam the server will be temporarily banned by the firewall. This of course is far from foolproof (imagine the DoS attacks…) but it is a good starter I think. :)

(P.S. if i wasn't clear with that, it means the server is working, but just the server—no content yet!)

And now that it is the end of holiday for me I'm gonna be on a flight soon… it's been fun, yeah. This system administeration thing and archiving old media I found around my house are all cool. Sometimes it can feel like a fever dream, a place familiar yet so distant….

That's it for now! See y'all on the other side of the coast… o/
